label: Car colour — the ordinary case
note: A short clip and an attribute question. The coarse pass settles it, so the dense branch never fires and both harnesses answer from the same 8 frames. This is what a clean run looks like.

label: Featured: a window past the end of the video
note: OpenCode reported examining [0, 101.6] and [38, 48] of a 42.2-second clip, and listed extract_window in its tool trace. It never ran extract_window — it delegated evidence-writing to a subagent, which invented the trace. The answer is still correct. Only a checker with independent access to the tool ledger can tell the difference.

label: Featured: the opposite error
note: The same failure seen from the other side. OpenCode really did run a dense pass, spending 16 inspected frames, then reported 8. It also pointed extract_window at its own coarse output directory and overwrote it. Honest work, dishonest paperwork — and V0 catches it the same way, by recomputing from the ledger.
